content.title: Reducing Cross-Script Contract Search Failures in KlozuraPro

facts.text: The company estimates that script mismatch affects roughly one in five searches, based on a January 2024 server-log sample.

sources.quote: We estimated this affects roughly one in five searches based on a sample we pulled from server logs in January 2024.

sources.quote: PostgreSQL with full-text search for document storage
Python-based NLP pipeline (spaCy, custom fine-tuned transformer models trained on Serbian-language contracts)

there are edge cases where the same Latin sequence maps to different Cyrillic letters depending on dialect conventions.
does not slow down search response times noticeably.

capacity for roughly one external project at a time alongside normal product development.

sources.quote: Trenutno je angažovan na dva aktivna projekta, ali ima kapaciteta za jedan manji industrijski ugovor ili konsultantski angažman.

facts.text: Dragić's work maps tokens to phoneme-based canonical forms for retrieval and evaluates this approach on manually annotated relevance pairs from Serbian court decisions.

sources.quote: the resulting phoneme string serves as the canonical form for retrieval purposes.
We evaluated the approach on a manually annotated gold standard of 4 200 query–document relevance pairs drawn from a legal corpus of 38 000 court decisions.

facts.text: His latency study reports an accuracy–latency tradeoff: transformer normalization achieved MRR 0.68 but added 47 ms at the 99th percentile on its tested workload.

sources.quote: The transformer-based normalizer achieves MRR of 0.68 but adds 47 ms at the 99th percentile.

inferences: This suggests a focused joint project could resolve normalization placement rather than rebuild search. The proposal is conditional because Dragić's availability is unconfirmed and his stated capacity is limited to a small engagement.

Court-decision results suggest methodological relevance, not validation for contracts or PostgreSQL. Canonicalization could conflate names, abbreviations or legal terms; representative relevance judgments and exception tests are therefore important.

The historical failure estimate may combine script mismatch with parsing or other failures. Reviewing successful and unsuccessful searches should help distinguish these explanations rather than assuming every zero-hit query has the same cause.
proposedActions: Use authorized contracts and randomly sampled current query occurrences; split tuning/evaluation, checking document/query-family independence. Compare unchanged PostgreSQL, indexing-only, query-only and both normalization, holding parsing, ranking and load constant. Judge all evaluation queries, including nonzero results; evaluate overall and separate held-out cross-script, mixed-script and ambiguous-mapping populations. Select the best configuration on tuning data. Proposed negotiable gates for overall evaluation and each population: 95% upper confidence bound ≤5% for zero hits despite an accessible relevant document; 95% lower bound on P@10 change ≥−2 percentage points; 95% upper confidence bounds on each p95/p99 relative latency increase ≤5% under company-approved representative load. Count each query occurrence once without deduplication; divide failures by all evaluated occurrences in that population. Treat unresolved relevance cases as failures and use conservative precision bounds. Go only with sufficient evidence, verified PostgreSQL/Python compatibility and delivery within the six-week engineering allocation; missing evaluation data or insufficient precision leaves the decision unresolved.

Propose a six-week schedule: week one for permissions, baseline reconstruction and acceptance definitions; weeks two–three for prototypes and tuning; weeks four–five for frozen evaluation and load tests; week six for a deployment decision. The company engineer would implement integration and workload replay; company reviewers would judge relevance. Dragić would propose normalization rules, experimental controls and error analysis, subject to confirmed hours.

Keep the initial prototype deterministic to limit integration scope; test ambiguous mappings, foreign names, abbreviations and within-token mixtures explicitly. A null result for either normalization location alone would not rule out a joint effect. Record index growth, rebuild time and maintenance effort; agree exception-rule ownership and rollback procedures. Neural fallback would be a separately justified follow-up because its reported accuracy gains carry latency costs.
questions: Can Dragić confirm a start date and weekly contribution for a small joint project within the company's six-week engineering window?
What authorized contract corpus, current logs and company relevance reviewers can support independent tuning and evaluation under the applicable confidentiality restrictions?
What numerical acceptance limits and representative load should define noticeable latency, relevance preservation, mixed-script robustness, index growth and reindexing downtime?
What budget, test environment, PostgreSQL configuration and maintenance arrangement can support the proposed scope?

content.markdown:
# Reducing Cross-Script Contract Search Failures in KlozuraPro

## Verified facts
- The company estimates that script mismatch affects roughly one in five searches, based on a January 2024 server-log sample. [F1]
- The company's existing stack includes PostgreSQL full-text search and a Python NLP pipeline using spaCy and Serbian-contract transformer models. [F2]
- The company identifies mixed-script robustness, dialect-dependent transliteration ambiguity and search response time as concerns. [F3]
- The company reports one backend engineer available for up to six weeks and capacity for roughly one external project alongside product development. [F4]
- Dragić's notes report two active projects and capacity for one smaller industrial contract or consulting engagement. [F5]
- Dragić's work maps tokens to phoneme-based canonical forms for retrieval and evaluates this approach on manually annotated relevance pairs from Serbian court decisions. [F6]
- His latency study reports an accuracy–latency tradeoff: transformer normalization achieved MRR 0.68 but added 47 ms at the 99th percentile on its tested workload. [F7]

## Potential benefits
- For the company: The experiment could identify where normalization belongs and whether it reduces confirmed cross-script failures without unacceptable relevance or latency costs.
- For the researcher: Subject to agreement and authorized access, Dragić could test how phoneme-based normalization transfers from court decisions to contract retrieval, using judged queries and controlled PostgreSQL comparisons.

## Our inference
- This suggests a focused joint project could resolve normalization placement rather than rebuild search. The proposal is conditional because Dragić's availability is unconfirmed and his stated capacity is limited to a small engagement.
- Court-decision results suggest methodological relevance, not validation for contracts or PostgreSQL. Canonicalization could conflate names, abbreviations or legal terms; representative relevance judgments and exception tests are therefore important.
- The historical failure estimate may combine script mismatch with parsing or other failures. Reviewing successful and unsuccessful searches should help distinguish these explanations rather than assuming every zero-hit query has the same cause.

## Proposed next steps
- Use authorized contracts and randomly sampled current query occurrences; split tuning/evaluation, checking document/query-family independence. Compare unchanged PostgreSQL, indexing-only, query-only and both normalization, holding parsing, ranking and load constant. Judge all evaluation queries, including nonzero results; evaluate overall and separate held-out cross-script, mixed-script and ambiguous-mapping populations. Select the best configuration on tuning data. Proposed negotiable gates for overall evaluation and each population: 95% upper confidence bound ≤5% for zero hits despite an accessible relevant document; 95% lower bound on P@10 change ≥−2 percentage points; 95% upper confidence bounds on each p95/p99 relative latency increase ≤5% under company-approved representative load. Count each query occurrence once without deduplication; divide failures by all evaluated occurrences in that population. Treat unresolved relevance cases as failures and use conservative precision bounds. Go only with sufficient evidence, verified PostgreSQL/Python compatibility and delivery within the six-week engineering allocation; missing evaluation data or insufficient precision leaves the decision unresolved.
- Propose a six-week schedule: week one for permissions, baseline reconstruction and acceptance definitions; weeks two–three for prototypes and tuning; weeks four–five for frozen evaluation and load tests; week six for a deployment decision. The company engineer would implement integration and workload replay; company reviewers would judge relevance. Dragić would propose normalization rules, experimental controls and error analysis, subject to confirmed hours.
- Keep the initial prototype deterministic to limit integration scope; test ambiguous mappings, foreign names, abbreviations and within-token mixtures explicitly. A null result for either normalization location alone would not rule out a joint effect. Record index growth, rebuild time and maintenance effort; agree exception-rule ownership and rollback procedures. Neural fallback would be a separately justified follow-up because its reported accuracy gains carry latency costs.

## Open questions
- Can Dragić confirm a start date and weekly contribution for a small joint project within the company's six-week engineering window?
- What authorized contract corpus, current logs and company relevance reviewers can support independent tuning and evaluation under the applicable confidentiality restrictions?
- What numerical acceptance limits and representative load should define noticeable latency, relevance preservation, mixed-script robustness, index growth and reindexing downtime?
- What budget, test environment, PostgreSQL configuration and maintenance arrangement can support the proposed scope?
